title: Membranous nephropathy
diseaseDescription: Bounded primary membranous nephropathy map. PLA2R1, THSD7A and the further reported podocyte target antigens are lumped into one shared antigen-autoantibody mechanism because the inspected evidence describes the same route: IgG4-predominant autoantibodies against a podocyte antigen, subepithelial immune deposits, glomerular complement activation and slit-diaphragm injury with nephrotic proteinuria. Secondary membranous nephropathy, therapy efficacy, diagnostic validation and antigen-specific clinical associations are outside this scope, and the relative importance of the complement initiation and effector routes is contested in the cited evidence.
releaseNote: Overall scientific summary of membranous-nephropathy-appraised-candidate-a3f88eef204e; external current-literature review remains pending. Provisional automatic appraisal of membranous-nephropathy-candidate-7ce925c46588. Automatic conservative metadata appraisal. Source entailment, study quality, broad disease coverage, circuit causation and independent replication require review. Confidence is capped at 1/4 until explicit editorial appraisal; therapeutic categories describe curated target coverage, not efficacy. No calibration or human approval is asserted. Independent review and calibration remain pending.

entities.label: PLA2R1
entities.description: The M-type phospholipase A2 receptor expressed by podocytes and identified as the dominant target antigen in the inspected primary membranous nephropathy cohorts. Human, mouse-transgenic and chimeric constructs are distinct experimental identities.

entities.label: THSD7A
entities.description: Thrombospondin type-1 domain-containing 7A, the second established podocyte target antigen; patient autoantibody findings and rodent anti-THSD7A antibody transfer are separate assertions.

entities.label: Further podocyte target antigens (SEMA3B, HTRA1 and additional putative targets)
entities.description: A lumped identity for the non-PLA2R1, non-THSD7A, non-NELL-1 target antigens reported in the inspected studies, including semaphorin 3B, serine protease HTRA1 and seven putative mass-spectrometry targets. NELL-1 is curated as its own entity because external review found it a major named antigen rather than a marginal one. Lumping reflects a shared antigen-autoantibody route; it does not assert that these antigens share frequency, serology, age distribution or clinical associations, and current literature increasingly treats antigen-defined subtypes as partly distinct clinicopathologic entities.

entities.label: Anti-podocyte-antigen IgG4 autoantibodies
entities.description: Circulating IgG, predominantly IgG4, reactive with podocyte target antigens in the inspected cohorts. Rodent experiments used heterologous rabbit or mouse antibodies rather than patient IgG unless stated.

entities.label: Podocyte
entities.description: The glomerular visceral epithelial cell expressing the target antigens; human biopsy tissue, cultured human podocytes and transgenic rodent podocytes are distinguished by each claim.

entities.label: Subepithelial immune deposits
entities.description: Granular antigen-IgG deposits in the subepithelial space along the glomerular basement membrane, detected by immunofluorescence, immunohistochemistry, mass spectrometry or electron microscopy.

entities.label: Classical complement pathway activation
entities.description: Classical-pathway activation detected in membranous nephropathy biopsy tissue; detection of components and proximity signals is distinct from demonstrated pathogenic necessity.

entities.label: Lectin complement pathway activation
entities.description: Mannose-binding-lectin-initiated activation, examined in human biopsies and in human podocyte culture with patient IgG4.

entities.label: Alternative complement pathway activation
entities.description: Factor-B-dependent amplification, assessed here mainly in a factor-B-null mouse model of subepithelial immune-complex disease.

entities.label: Glomerular complement C3 activation
entities.description: C3-dependent complement activation at the glomerular filtration barrier, probed by C3-deficient animals and C3 silencing.

entities.label: C3a / C3a receptor signalling
entities.description: The C3a anaphylatoxin and its podocyte receptor, examined by receptor antagonism and gene silencing.

entities.label: C5b-9 membrane attack complex
entities.description: The terminal complement complex assembled on podocyte membranes; its necessity differed between the inspected models.

entities.label: Slit-diaphragm proteins (nephrin, NEPH1, synaptopodin)
entities.description: Integral podocyte slit-diaphragm and associated cytoskeletal proteins whose loss or proteolysis was measured in the inspected models.

entities.label: Nephrotic-range proteinuria and nephrotic syndrome
entities.description: The study-defined proteinuric and nephrotic outcome, covering human biopsy-proven disease and rodent albuminuria; it is not a validated diagnostic or prognostic endpoint here.

entities.label: HLA-DQA1 risk allele
entities.description: The chromosome 6p21 HLA-DQA1 risk allele reported in a white-ancestry genome-wide association study of biopsy-proven idiopathic membranous nephropathy.

entities.label: B and T lymphocytes
entities.description: Mature adaptive lymphocytes, absent in the Rag2-deficient animals used to test whether autoantibody production is required for disease.

entities.label: NELL-1
entities.description: Neural tissue encoding protein with EGF-like repeats, a separately named podocyte target antigen in PLA2R-negative membranous nephropathy. It is kept distinct from the lumped putative-antigen identity because it accounts for a materially larger share of cases.

entities.label: PLA2R epitope spreading beyond the CysR domain
entities.description: Extension of the anti-PLA2R1 response from the cysteine-rich domain to the CTLD1 and CTLD7 domains, measured by domain-specific ELISA in patient sera.

entities.label: Complement-fixing IgG subclasses (IgG1-IgG3)
entities.description: Antigen-specific IgG subclasses other than IgG4 found alongside the IgG4-predominant response. Their presence bears on the classical-pathway question because IgG4 does not fix C1q; this map records their presence only, not a demonstrated pathway contribution.

claims.text: Anti-PLA2R autoantibodies in the inspected idiopathic membranous nephropathy sera were mainly IgG4, matching the predominant immunoglobulin subclass of the glomerular deposits.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Subclass predominance is an association, not evidence that IgG4 alone causes injury.
Reported in 26 of 37 idiopathic cases; this is not whole-disease coverage.

claims.text: PLA2R was expressed in podocytes of normal human glomeruli and colocalized with IgG4 in the glomerular immune deposits of patients with membranous nephropathy.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Colocalization does not establish that antibody binding to this antigen initiates the lesion.

claims.text: IgG eluted from the glomerular deposits of idiopathic, but not lupus membranous or IgA nephropathy, cases recognized PLA2R.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Eluate reactivity establishes antigen presence in the deposits, not the sequence or sufficiency of deposit formation.

claims.text: Circulating autoantibodies to THSD7A without anti-PLA2R1 reactivity were found in 15 of 154 patients with idiopathic membranous nephropathy, defining a distinct seronegative-for-PLA2R1 subgroup.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
A small antigen subgroup; frequency outside these two cohorts is not established.
Mutual exclusivity with anti-PLA2R1 in this cohort does not exclude double positivity elsewhere.

claims.text: THSD7A localized to podocytes in patient biopsy samples, and IgG eluted from one sample was specific for THSD7A.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
The eluate result rests on a single sample.

claims.text: Semaphorin 3B colocalized with IgG in granular glomerular basement membrane deposits of PLA2R-negative membranous nephropathy cases.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Eleven cases in total, mostly pediatric; this is not an adult primary membranous nephropathy frequency estimate.

claims.text: Sera from four of four patients with active semaphorin 3B-associated disease reacted with reduced semaphorin 3B, while the single patient in clinical remission and control sera did not.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Five sera only, and reactivity was to the reduced antigen, unlike the conformation-dependent reactivity reported for PLA2R1 and THSD7A.
Remission in one patient cannot establish that antibody level tracks activity.

claims.text: Anti-HTRA1 antibodies were predominantly IgG4, as reported for PLA2R- and THSD7A-associated disease.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
The authors infer a primary etiology from subclass; subclass alone does not establish that inference.
Prevalence was 4.2% among 118 quadruple-negative biopsy specimens.

claims.text: HTRA1 was specifically detected within the immune deposits of HTRA1-associated membranous nephropathy in 14 patients across three cohorts.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Detection within deposits does not establish that anti-HTRA1 antibody binding caused those deposits.

claims.text: Seven further putative antigens were recovered from immune complexes in quadruple-negative membranous nephropathy biopsy tissue, each colocalizing with IgG in the deposits.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
The authors label these putative; no circulating autoantibody against them was demonstrated here.
The cohort included membranous lupus nephritis, which is outside this map’s primary-disease scope.

claims.text: Frequencies of the putative antigens in consecutive case series ranged from under 1% to 4.9%, and two were positive only in their index cases, qualifying how much disease these targets explain.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Index-case-only positivity leaves these targets unreplicated.

claims.text: In a 270-patient biopsy-proven cohort the non-PLA2R antigens were rare and semaphorin 3B-associated disease was not found at all, qualifying the share of disease attributable to the lumped minor antigens.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
A single-centre adult cohort; absence of semaphorin 3B is consistent with its reported pediatric predominance rather than disproving that entity.
The report also found malignancy or systemic autoimmunity in many septuple-negative patients, which falls outside this primary-disease scope.

claims.text: Strong glomerular PLA2R staining tracked the presence of serum PLA2R autoantibodies in a prospective cohort of 88 patients with membranous nephropathy.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
A correlation between two measurements of the same antigen-antibody system, not an independent mechanism.
Twelve antibody-negative patients remained unexplained in the report.

claims.text: PLA2R immunostaining was also faintly positive in normal kidneys and in other glomerular injuries, so antigen presence alone does not mark the disease.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Faint baseline expression limits any diagnostic reading of antigen staining alone.

claims.text: Homozygosity for both the HLA-DQA1 and PLA2R1 risk alleles carried an odds ratio of 78.5 for idiopathic membranous nephropathy in white-ancestry cohorts.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Restricted to white ancestry; the estimate does not transfer to other populations.
The odds ratio applies to combined homozygosity, is wide in its confidence interval, and genetic association is not a mechanism.

claims.text: The chromosome 2q24 locus containing the PLA2R1 gene was independently associated with idiopathic membranous nephropathy in the same genome-wide analysis.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
A locus association; the cached passage does not establish which variant or mechanism is responsible.

claims.text: Mice expressing full-length human PLA2R1 in podocytes spontaneously developed anti-human PLA2R1 antibodies, nephrotic syndrome with progressive albuminuria and the typical morphological signs of membranous nephropathy.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
A transgenic xeno-antigen model; spontaneous autoimmunity against a human protein in mice is not the human loss of tolerance.
Mouse albuminuria is not interchangeable with human nephrotic syndrome.

claims.text: In the same model, murine IgG formed granular glomerular deposits with subepithelial electron-dense material, matching the deposit pattern of human disease.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Deposit morphology in a transgenic mouse does not establish the deposit kinetics or composition of human disease.

claims.text: Human-PLA2R1-expressing mice lacking mature B and T lymphocytes developed neither anti-PLA2R1 antibodies nor proteinuria, indicating that the disease in this model requires an adaptive antibody response.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Rag2 deficiency removes both B and T cells, so the experiment does not separate their contributions.
Demonstrated in the transgenic mouse model, not in patients.

claims.text: In a chimeric PLA2R1 active-immunization model, C3-deficient mice developed substantially less severe albuminuria and nephrotic syndrome than C3-competent mice.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Disease was attenuated but not abolished, so C3 is contributory rather than shown to be necessary.
Active immunization against a chimeric antigen is an induced model, not spontaneous human autoimmunity.

claims.text: Proximity ligation assays in membranous nephropathy biopsies showed complement assembly dominated by the classical pathway, correlating with the degree of glomerular C1q-binding IgG subclasses.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Tissue assembly signals and subclass correlation do not establish which pathway initiates injury in each patient.
This dominance conflicts with model evidence assigning the decisive role to other pathways; the disagreement is unresolved.

claims.text: Components of the lectin pathway were among those found in membranous nephropathy renal biopsies.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Component presence is not pathway necessity.

claims.text: Components of the alternative pathway were likewise found in membranous nephropathy renal biopsies.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Component presence is not pathway necessity.

claims.text: In an antigen-specific autoimmune mouse model, severe disease with extensive loss of the slit-diaphragm proteins nephrin and neph1 occurred only in complement-competent animals.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Mouse slit-diaphragm protein loss is a model readout, not a measured human outcome.
Complement deficiency in this comparison is not resolved to a single pathway.

claims.text: Mice lacking factor B failed to develop albuminuria or glomerular C3c and C5b-9 deposition after subepithelial immune complexes formed, indicating that alternative-pathway amplification drove complement activation in this model.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
A heterologous mouse immune-complex model, not an antigen-specific primary disease model.
This assigns necessity to the alternative pathway, which the human tissue proximity-assay evidence does not support.

claims.text: Glomerular IgG deposition was similar in wild-type and factor-B-null mice, so the alternative pathway affected complement activation downstream of deposit formation rather than deposition itself.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
This is a mouse observation; the evidence type is recorded as observational within that experiment rather than an intervention on deposition.

claims.text: Albuminuria was reduced but not completely abolished in C5-deficient mice, so terminal-pathway activity contributed only partly to proteinuria in this model.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Incomplete protection shows a partial contribution and leaves C5-independent proteinuria unexplained.

claims.text: Anti-PLA2R1 IgG4 bound mannose-binding lectin directly in a glycosylation-dependent manner, and patient galactose-deficient IgG4 levels correlated with anti-PLA2R1 titres and with podocyte damage induced by those sera.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
A culture system with patient IgG4; it does not establish that the lectin pathway predominates in patient kidneys.

claims.text: Specific blockade of the lectin pathway prevented the degradation of synaptopodin and NEPH1 caused by patient IgG4 in the presence of complement.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Cultured human podocytes with exogenous complement; the result does not quantify the pathway’s contribution in vivo.

claims.text: Assembly of terminal C5b-9 was required for the proteolysis of synaptopodin and NEPH1 in this podocyte model.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Requirement in this culture system conflicts with the glomerulus-on-a-chip result in which membrane-attack-complex inhibition did not change albumin permselectivity.

claims.text: Activation of the complement receptors C3aR1 or C5aR1 was likewise required for the proteolysis of synaptopodin and NEPH1 in the same podocyte model.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
The cached sentence pairs C3aR1 with C5aR1; this map does not separate the two receptors.

claims.text: A C3aR antagonist prevented proteinuria in a mouse model of membranous nephropathy, supporting the chip-based finding that C3a/C3aR signalling drives injury.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Pharmacological antagonism in a mouse model; this is not clinical efficacy evidence and therapies are outside this map.

claims.text: Inhibiting membrane-attack-complex formation did not affect albumin permselectivity in the glomerulus-on-a-chip model, contradicting the view that C5b-9 is the principal effector of proteinuria.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
A chip model of albumin permselectivity, not whole-kidney proteinuria.
This result stands against the C5-deficient mouse and podocyte-culture evidence for a terminal-complex contribution.

claims.text: Anti-THSD7A antibodies caused significant loss of the slit-diaphragm proteins nephrin and NEPH1 in wild-type mice without transcriptional downregulation.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Heterologous rabbit antibody transfer, not patient IgG4.

claims.text: Podocyte-specific Thsd7a-knockout mice were completely protected from disease after anti-THSD7A antibody transfer, establishing antigen dependence in this model.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Antigen dependence in a mouse antibody-transfer model does not establish the human initiating event.

claims.text: In C3-deficient mice, proteolytic activation and slit-diaphragm protein loss still occurred, showing that these changes were driven by complement-independent pathways in this model.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Directly opposes the complement-dependent slit-protein loss reported in the antigen-specific autoimmune model; the conflict is unresolved.

claims.text: Reactive epitopes were identified in the cysteine-rich, C-type lectin domain 1 and C-type lectin domain 7 regions of PLA2R1, allowing patients to be stratified by domain profile.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Domain mapping in one cohort; epitope definitions are assay-dependent.

claims.text: High anti-PLA2R1 activity and epitope spreading beyond the cysteine-rich epitope were independent risk factors for poor renal prognosis, while anti-CysR-restricted patients had less nephrotic-range proteinuria and higher spontaneous remission.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
An observational prognostic association in a single cohort of 69 patients; it does not establish that spreading causes progression.

claims.text: Although all 117 patients carried antigen-specific IgG4 antibodies, IgG3, IgG1 and IgG2 antibodies were also present in 87%, 72% and 26% of patients, so the response is IgG4-predominant rather than IgG4-exclusive.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Subclass presence is recorded; this report does not measure complement activation by those subclasses.
The cohort includes malignancy-associated cases, which are outside this map’s primary-disease scope.

claims.text: Subclass distribution did not differ between primary and cancer-associated disease and showed no association with disease outcome, so subclass profile did not stratify patients in this cohort.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
A null result in 117 patients; it does not exclude a subclass effect in larger or differently powered cohorts.

claims.text: NELL-1 and IgG colocalized in granular glomerular basement membrane deposits of PLA2R-negative membranous nephropathy.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Colocalization does not establish that anti-NELL-1 antibody binding initiates the deposits.

claims.text: NELL-1 was positive in 29 of 126 PLA2R-negative cases, and the clinical and biopsy findings of NELL-1-positive disease showed features of primary membranous nephropathy, so NELL-1 is a substantial named antigen within the primary group rather than a marginal putative target.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
A share of PLA2R-negative cases, not of all membranous nephropathy; other series report NELL-1 in malignancy-associated disease, which is outside this scope.

claims.text: Sera from five NELL-1-positive patients reacted with NELL-1, with no reactivity in control sera.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Five sera only; no validated serological assay or titre relationship is established here.

claims.text: Anti-PLA2R antibody levels correlated strongly with clinical status and proteinuria across serial samples from patients at different disease stages.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
Eighteen patients and a semiquantitative Western blot assay; the correlation is within-cohort and does not establish a monitoring threshold.
Repeated samples from the same patients are not independent observations.
The cached passage stops before the reported statistics because the repository source normalizer removes text from the less-than sign of "P < 0.01" onward; the source reports r = 0.73, P < 0.01.

claims.text: Median ELISA titres measured against full-length PLA2R1 did not differ significantly between the domain-reactivity subgroups, so total titre alone did not carry the prognostic separation.
limitations: Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending.
A null comparison in a small stratified cohort; absence of a difference is not evidence of equivalence.

evidenceItems.studySystem: Complement-component detection across all three pathways in membranous nephropathy renal biopsies in the same report

evidenceItems.summary: In an antigen-specific autoimmune mouse model, severe disease with extensive loss of the slit-diaphragm proteins nephrin and neph1 occurred only in complement-competent animals.
evidenceItems.location: Europe PMC abstract of the primary report; Results or Conclusions sentence
evidenceItems.studySystem: Antigen-specific autoimmune mouse model of membranous nephropathy comparing complement-deficient mice with wild-type littermates, plus RNA-interference silencing of C3 after proteinuria onset

evidenceItems.summary: Mice lacking factor B failed to develop albuminuria or glomerular C3c and C5b-9 deposition after subepithelial immune complexes formed, indicating that alternative-pathway amplification drove complement activation in this model.
evidenceItems.location: Europe PMC abstract of the primary report; Results or Conclusions sentence
evidenceItems.studySystem: Mouse model of subepithelial immune-complex formation compared between wild-type, factor-B-null and C5-deficient mice

evidenceItems.summary: Glomerular IgG deposition was similar in wild-type and factor-B-null mice, so the alternative pathway affected complement activation downstream of deposit formation rather than deposition itself.
evidenceItems.location: Europe PMC abstract of the primary report; Results or Conclusions sentence
evidenceItems.studySystem: Comparison of glomerular IgG deposition between wild-type and factor-B-null mice in the same report

evidenceItems.summary: Albuminuria was reduced but not completely abolished in C5-deficient mice, so terminal-pathway activity contributed only partly to proteinuria in this model.
evidenceItems.location: Europe PMC abstract of the primary report; Results or Conclusions sentence
evidenceItems.studySystem: C5-deficient mice in the same subepithelial immune-complex model

evidenceItems.summary: Anti-PLA2R1 IgG4 bound mannose-binding lectin directly in a glycosylation-dependent manner, and patient galactose-deficient IgG4 levels correlated with anti-PLA2R1 titres and with podocyte damage induced by those sera.
evidenceItems.location: Europe PMC abstract of the primary report; Results or Conclusions sentence
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human podocyte culture model exposed to anti-PLA2R1-positive patient sera or isolated IgG4, with lectin-pathway blockade, plus glycosylation profiling in a patient cohort

evidenceItems.summary: Specific blockade of the lectin pathway prevented the degradation of synaptopodin and NEPH1 caused by patient IgG4 in the presence of complement.
evidenceItems.location: Europe PMC abstract of the primary report; Results or Conclusions sentence
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human podocyte cultures exposed to anti-PLA2R1-positive patient sera or isolated IgG4 with complement, with specific lectin-pathway blockade

evidenceItems.summary: Assembly of terminal C5b-9 was required for the proteolysis of synaptopodin and NEPH1 in this podocyte model.
evidenceItems.location: Europe PMC abstract of the primary report; Results or Conclusions sentence
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human podocyte cultures with patient IgG4 and complement, using terminal-complex and complement-receptor interventions

evidenceItems.summary: Activation of the complement receptors C3aR1 or C5aR1 was likewise required for the proteolysis of synaptopodin and NEPH1 in the same podocyte model.
evidenceItems.location: Europe PMC abstract of the primary report; Results or Conclusions sentence
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human podocyte cultures with patient IgG4 and complement, using terminal-complex and complement-receptor interventions

evidenceItems.summary: A C3aR antagonist prevented proteinuria in a mouse model of membranous nephropathy, supporting the chip-based finding that C3a/C3aR signalling drives injury.
evidenceItems.location: Europe PMC abstract of the primary report; Results or Conclusions sentence
evidenceItems.studySystem: Glomerulus-on-a-chip model of anti-PLA2R-induced human membranous nephropathy together with a mouse model treated with a C3aR antagonist

evidenceItems.summary: Inhibiting membrane-attack-complex formation did not affect albumin permselectivity in the glomerulus-on-a-chip model, contradicting the view that C5b-9 is the principal effector of proteinuria.
evidenceItems.location: Europe PMC abstract of the primary report; Results or Conclusions sentence
evidenceItems.studySystem: Primary human podocytes expressing PLA2R in a glomerulus-on-a-chip system exposed to membranous nephropathy serum, with membrane-attack-complex inhibition

evidenceItems.summary: Anti-THSD7A antibodies caused significant loss of the slit-diaphragm proteins nephrin and NEPH1 in wild-type mice without transcriptional downregulation.
evidenceItems.location: Europe PMC abstract of the primary report; Results or Conclusions sentence
evidenceItems.studySystem: Membranous nephropathy model induced in control and podocyte-specific Thsd7a-knockout mice with rabbit anti-THSD7A antibodies, analysed by transcriptome and proteome profiling

evidenceItems.summary: Podocyte-specific Thsd7a-knockout mice were completely protected from disease after anti-THSD7A antibody transfer, establishing antigen dependence in this model.
evidenceItems.location: Europe PMC abstract of the primary report; Results or Conclusions sentence
evidenceItems.studySystem: Podocyte-specific Thsd7a-knockout mice compared with controls after anti-THSD7A antibody transfer in the same report

evidenceItems.summary: In C3-deficient mice, proteolytic activation and slit-diaphragm protein loss still occurred, showing that these changes were driven by complement-independent pathways in this model.
evidenceItems.location: Europe PMC abstract of the primary report; Results or Conclusions sentence
evidenceItems.studySystem: Anti-THSD7A antibody transfer into C3-deficient mice with transcriptome and proteome analysis in the same report

evidenceItems.summary: Reactive epitopes were identified in the cysteine-rich, C-type lectin domain 1 and C-type lectin domain 7 regions of PLA2R1, allowing patients to be stratified by domain profile.
evidenceItems.location: Europe PMC abstract of the primary report; Results or Conclusions sentence
evidenceItems.studySystem: Serum screening of 50 PLA2R1-positive patients against PLA2R1 deletion mutants, then domain-specific ELISA stratification of 69 PLA2R1-positive patients

evidenceItems.summary: High anti-PLA2R1 activity and epitope spreading beyond the cysteine-rich epitope were independent risk factors for poor renal prognosis, while anti-CysR-restricted patients had less nephrotic-range proteinuria and higher spontaneous remission.
evidenceItems.location: Europe PMC abstract of the primary report; Results or Conclusions sentence
evidenceItems.studySystem: Multivariable Cox regression on 69 PLA2R1-positive patients stratified by domain reactivity and followed for renal outcome

evidenceItems.summary: Although all 117 patients carried antigen-specific IgG4 antibodies, IgG3, IgG1 and IgG2 antibodies were also present in 87%, 72% and 26% of patients, so the response is IgG4-predominant rather than IgG4-exclusive.
evidenceItems.location: Europe PMC abstract of the primary report; Results or Conclusions sentence
evidenceItems.studySystem: Western blot analysis of antigen-specific IgG subclasses in serum from 76 patients with PLA2R1-associated and 41 with THSD7A-associated membranous nephropathy, at baseline and during follow-up in 55

evidenceItems.summary: Subclass distribution did not differ between primary and cancer-associated disease and showed no association with disease outcome, so subclass profile did not stratify patients in this cohort.
evidenceItems.location: Europe PMC abstract of the primary report; Results or Conclusions sentence
evidenceItems.studySystem: Comparison of antigen-specific IgG subclass distribution between primary and malignancy-associated cases, and against disease outcome, in the same report

evidenceItems.summary: NELL-1 and IgG colocalized in granular glomerular basement membrane deposits of PLA2R-negative membranous nephropathy.
evidenceItems.location: Europe PMC abstract of the primary report; Results or Conclusions sentence
evidenceItems.studySystem: Laser microdissection and mass spectrometry of PLA2R-negative membranous nephropathy glomeruli, with immunohistochemistry in a 91-case discovery cohort and two European validation cohorts

evidenceItems.summary: NELL-1 was positive in 29 of 126 PLA2R-negative cases, and the clinical and biopsy findings of NELL-1-positive disease showed features of primary membranous nephropathy, so NELL-1 is a substantial named antigen within the primary group rather than a marginal putative target.
evidenceItems.location: Europe PMC abstract of the primary report; Results or Conclusions sentence
evidenceItems.studySystem: Clinical and biopsy characterisation of the NELL-1-positive cases identified across the discovery and validation cohorts in the same report

evidenceItems.summary: Sera from five NELL-1-positive patients reacted with NELL-1, with no reactivity in control sera.
evidenceItems.location: Europe PMC abstract of the primary report; Results or Conclusions sentence
evidenceItems.studySystem: Western blot of five available patient sera against NELL-1, with control sera, in the same report

evidenceItems.summary: Anti-PLA2R antibody levels correlated strongly with clinical status and proteinuria across serial samples from patients at different disease stages.
evidenceItems.location: Europe PMC abstract of the primary report; Results or Conclusions sentence
evidenceItems.studySystem: Blinded Western blot immunoassay of 54 serum samples from 18 European patients with idiopathic membranous nephropathy collected at various clinical stages

evidenceItems.summary: Median ELISA titres measured against full-length PLA2R1 did not differ significantly between the domain-reactivity subgroups, so total titre alone did not carry the prognostic separation.
evidenceItems.location: Europe PMC abstract of the primary report; Results or Conclusions sentence
evidenceItems.studySystem: Full-length PLA2R1 ELISA titres compared across the CysR, CysRC1 and CysRC1C7 subgroups in the same report

mapViews.label: Antigen-antibody, complement and podocyte injury in primary membranous nephropathy

scientificSummary.scope: Bounded primary (autoantibody-mediated) membranous nephropathy map: podocyte target antigens (PLA2R1, THSD7A and other recently described antigens) lumped as one shared antigen-antibody mechanism, subepithelial immune-complex formation, complement activation, podocyte injury and nephrotic proteinuria. Secondary membranous nephropathy (lupus, malignancy, infection, drug-associated) and therapy efficacy are excluded.

paragraphs.text: Anti-PLA2R antibody levels correlated strongly with clinical status and proteinuria across serial samples from patients at different disease stages. Mice expressing full-length human PLA2R1 in podocytes spontaneously developed anti-human PLA2R1 antibodies, nephrotic syndrome with progressive albuminuria and the typical morphological signs of membranous nephropathy. NELL-1 was positive in 29 of 126 PLA2R-negative cases, and the clinical and biopsy findings of NELL-1-positive disease showed features of primary membranous nephropathy, so NELL-1 is a substantial named antigen within the primary group rather than a marginal putative target.

These selected findings describe a bounded candidate, whose overall explanation has not been independently checked against current literature. Agent-inspected abstract only; full methods, cohort independence and figures were not reviewed, and independent domain review is pending. Eighteen patients and a semiquantitative Western blot assay; the correlation is within-cohort and does not establish a monitoring threshold. Treatment efficacy has not been synthesized in this summary.
